_comment: Copy to pipeline/character/<video>/plan.json. The locked plan, the only input of production. Written by the planning system (video-lock) or by hand, then approved by the user. No production stage edits it. A plan without schema_version is a legacy (v1) plan: only the fields from video_id to approved below exist, and it runs as before. A v2 plan (schema_version 2) adds revision, editorial, the beat fields from id to item_index (and reaction), overlays, assets, narrators, reaction_refs and publishing_note, and is checked by scripts/character/bridge.py; its approval is planning-approval.json beside it (planning-approval.example.json). The contract is plan.schema.json. A v2 plan may leave characters, set and outfit empty when no generated person or mascot appears. No value in angle brackets survives locking.

editorial.filming_format: talking_head | hook_to_demo | live_use | before_after | text_over_action | voiceover_action (face_to_demo is read as hook_to_demo)

hook.channel: spoken | visual | text | spoken_visual | text_visual | reaction (a silent reacting face with the hook as a text overlay; never spoken)

editorial.recipe_id: pitch_proof | discovery_demo | routine_log | personal_note | state_change | explain_action | list_steps | setup_reveal
editorial.close: none | payoff | save | share | follow | question | profile | product_action
editorial.series: standalone, or {kind: progress_log, series_id, subject_ids, routine_id, episode, day, previous_plan_ref, state_fact_refs}

experiment.axis: none | hook | proof | product_presence | close | cast

script.speaker: <character id, or vo (the beat's narrator)>
script.delivery: <which word lifts, where it slows, the breath>

beats.action: <what is visible: her face reacts, silent>

reaction._comment: A silent reaction (segment X): the handle's own face performs these written beats; no line, no voice, no lip sync. null while no reference is found: production waits.

beats.role: <the recipe's beat: attention, problem, item, result...>
beats.end_s: <seconds; beats meet end to start and cover the length>
beats.action: <what is visible, copied word for word into the shot's action by P1>
subject_ids: <world.json fixed subject; source:<name> for a subject only in a supplied clip>
beats.framing: face | hands_only | subject_only | app_screen (the real app full frame: R or P)

panels.asset_id: <asset id, or null for a generated B panel>

overlays.role: hook | paragraph | step_label | comparison_label | day_counter | source_credit
overlays._fact_refs: the facts the text states; required when the text has a digit (not for step_label or day_counter)

assets.origin: own_camera | user_supplied | licensed | permitted_reference | verified_expert | app_recording
assets.permission_ref: <licence or permission; required unless own_camera or app_recording>
assets.paired_input_ref: <for a screen of a live demonstration: {asset_id, input_t_s, output_t_s}, else null>

reaction_refs._comment: A real reference reaction from the user's research. It gives the written performance only; its clip is never a generation input (generation_input true is refused).
reaction_refs.notes_ref: <the notes that describe it, or null>

hero_strings.<screen id>: <the one string the viewer must read>

publishing_note.caption: <optional>
publishing_note.music_note: <a note only; the file stays music-free>

source: <a reference post, or a research brief>
